function: Learned joint selection of finite-codebook BS precoder, quantized RIS phase shifts and user combiners maximizing sum effective capacity under statistical QoS constraints (pp. 2-3, Eq. 9).
system: Downlink RIS-aided holographic MIMO: BS surface L=64 sampling points, passive reflecting RIS N=64 elements (2-bit), U=4 users with 2 antennas, 10 MHz, carrier not stated (pp. 2, 4).
method: Discrete softmax policy gradient deep RL with a generative diffusion model as policy network (15 denoising steps), state-dependent baseline, Adam, 5000 training episodes (pp. 3-4, Table I).
data_channel: Own simulator: correlated Rician fading (K-factor 10 dB) on all links with exponential spatial correlation, random unit-norm codebooks; no standard channel model or dataset (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Training: 5000 episodes, default U=4, N=64, QoS exponent 0.02 (p. 4). Testing: sweeps of QoS exponent and RIS elements 8 to 512; held-out conditions not stated (p. 5).
baselines: Learned only: DDPG and DQN with fully connected networks, trained on the same environment (p. 4); no non-learned or optimization baseline appears in Figs. 2-4 (p. 5).
metrics: Average reward per episode, average effective capacity per user (bps/Hz) versus QoS exponent and RIS elements; percentage gains over DDPG and DQN (pp. 4-5, Figs. 2-4).
complexity: Per-iteration order O(B(T d^2 + U Nr L)); GDM sampling and backpropagation O(T d^2), T diffusion steps, width d, batch B (Eq. 21, p. 4).
q1_support: p. 2: "All links follow correlated Rician fading". Custom Rician model with exponential correlation (Table I, p. 4: K-factor 10 dB); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "Fig. 4 evaluates scalability by varying the number of RIS elements". Performance sweeps only: Fig. 3 varies the QoS exponent and Fig. 4 the RIS size, but the paper never states that a policy trained under one setting is tested under another (Table I, p. 4: one training setup).
q3_support: p. 4: "For comparison, we consider DDPG and DQN frameworks". Both are learned baselines; no non-learned method (optimization, fixed or random RIS) is simulated in Figs. 2-4, although the conclusion (p. 5) mentions optimization baselines.
q4_support: p. 4: "Overall, the per-iteration cost is". Eq. 21 gives O(B(T d^2 + U Nr L)) with T diffusion steps, hidden width d and batch size B, in the complexity analysis of Section III-B.
q5_support: p. 4: "the default simulation parameters are listed in Table I". Own Rician simulation with a parameter table only; no code or data link, DOI or public dataset appears in the paper.
notes: Included, area 3: the agent picks BS precoder, RIS phase shifts and user combiners from codebooks (pp. 2-3, Eq. 9); the RIS has 64 passive reflecting elements.
